claims.text: Coherently ordered L12 precipitates can be introduced within an fcc Fe-Co-Ni-Ti high-entropy-alloy matrix.
Introducing L12 precipitates will restore the orbital magnetic moment suppressed in the homogeneous fcc alloy.
Introducing L12 precipitates will produce a magnetic ground state with coercivity exceeding 100 Oe.
The initial single-phase fcc Fe-Co-Ni-Ti alloy has a homogeneous elemental distribution, a suppressed orbital moment, and coercivity below 10 Oe.
Isothermal annealing at 600–800 °C can induce coherent L12 precipitation in the proposed fcc Fe-Co-Ni-Ti matrix.
The intended precipitates can be Al3Ni- or Al3Co-type L12 phases.
B2 and Laves phases are brittle and should be avoided to prevent degradation of mechanical properties.
Magnetic ordering in the proposed alloy will be maintained over an operating range of 300–600 °C.
A suitable annealing window can stabilize L12 precipitates without their dissolution or the formation of B2/BCC phases.
Coherent L12 precipitates act as magnetic-domain-wall pinning centers.
Local lattice distortion around L12 precipitates enhances spin-orbit coupling.
The L12/fcc interface gives Ni and Co a higher orbital-moment contribution than they have in the homogeneous fcc matrix.
Restoration of orbital moment increases magnetocrystalline anisotropy and consequently coercivity.
Coherent L12/fcc interfaces provide strong domain-wall pinning that raises coercivity.
The dual-phase alloy will retain saturation magnetization comparable to or slightly below that of the single-phase alloy.
The dual-phase alloy will retain a magnetic ordering temperature well above room temperature.
A single-phase control annealed at 1000 °C for 15 hours has homogeneous elemental distribution and coercivity of 4.3 Oe.
The 1000 °C baseline is an fcc Fe-Co-Ni-Ti alloy, and its 4.3 Oe coercivity is caused by orbital-moment suppression.
Ti promotes B2 formation in Al-rich Fe-Co-Ni-based systems.

contradictions.description: The stated alloy and initial matrix contain Fe, Co, Ni, and Ti but no Al, while the intervention proposes forming Al3Ni or Al3Co precipitates without specifying any Al addition.

The mechanism gives both orbital-moment restoration and domain-wall pinning as routes to increased coercivity, but the falsification rule rejects the hypothesis whenever XMCD shows no orbital-moment increase, even if confirmed coherent precipitates raise coercivity through the separately proposed pinning mechanism.

The stated operating regime is 300–600 °C, but magnetic measurements are specified only at 300 K and 500 K (approximately 27 °C and 227 °C), so the experiment does not test the stated operating-temperature interval.
